title: Cattan, Rodrigues & Congedo 2019 — Passive Head-Mounted Display Music-Listening EEG dataset (PHMD)
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 12 healthy subjects during music listening with and without a passive head-mounted display (PHMD). A passive head-mounted display is a head-mounted device that does not include any electronics except for a smartphone. The study employed a 16-channel EEG system sampled at 512 Hz to investigate the effects of smartphone-integrated head-mounted displays on neural activity during auditory stimulation. Data were collected in a laboratory setting with alternating blocks of smartphone on/off conditions during passive listening to Bach compositions.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a 16-channel g.USBamp system (sampling rate: 512 Hz) with wet electrodes in a standard 10-20 montage. Subjects sat approximately 50 cm from a screen without noise-reduction devices. Each experimental block consisted of 60 seconds of recording with eyes open. Ten blocks were presented in randomized order, alternating between smartphone switched-off and switched-on conditions. Reference electrode was placed at the right earlobe with ground at AFz. Data were recorded without digital filtering using OpenViBE software.
